title: Rava bar Hamduri
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: So Yuchasin cites him, at the end of chapter 1 of Yevamot, as Shmuel’s student. Seder HaDorot already criticized it for misunderstanding the plain sense of the Gemara, since there Rava said, “Bar Hamduri explained it to me.” Hyman objects that Seder HaDorot overlooked an error in Yuchasin, for his name is not found in chapter 1 of Yevamot; he proposes chapter 17 of Shabbat, where it reads “Bar Hamduri said that Shmuel said.”

Dikdukei Soferim there cites a manuscript that writes “Rav bar Hamduri said that Shmuel said.” Hyman considers that Yuchasin undoubtedly had the reading “Rava said,” or it was written “Rav′ said”; from this Yuchasin derived, as is its way, that he was Shmuel’s student because he spoke in his name.

notes.text: The manuscript siglum א״פ remains literal, not a newly identified manuscript. Hyman’s locator correction, undoubtedly assertion and proposed Rava/Rav-apostrophe reconstruction retain their attribution and force.

The directly consulted Yevamot 83b:10 has Rava saying that Bar Hamduri explained it to him, keeping speaker and explainer distinct. It does not establish an individual named Rava bar Hamduri or verify Hyman’s proposed Shabbat chapter-17 locator. The Yuchasin, Seder HaDorot and Dikdukei Soferim claims and the manuscript siglum remain Hyman-attributed.
